facts: Tokyo was originally a small fishing village named Edo before becoming Japan's capital in 1868.
The world-famous Tokyo Marathon is one of the six prestigious World Marathon Majors.
Mount Fuji can be clearly seen from Tokyo's highest observation decks on crisp, clear days.
Tokyo features the world's busiest pedestrian crossing located right outside Shibuya Station.
The iconic Tokyo Tower was built in 1958 and inspired by the Eiffel Tower in Paris.
Tokyo Skytree is the tallest structure in Japan, offering breathtaking panoramic views of the metropolis.
Tokyo has more Michelin-starred restaurants than any other city in the entire world.
Ueno Park is famous for hosting over a thousand cherry blossom trees during springtime.
Running around the Imperial Palace perimeter is a legendary five-kilometer loop popular with local joggers.
Tokyo hosted the Summer Olympic Games twice, first in 1964 and later in 2021.
Traditional Japanese ramen is the ultimate post-run comfort food loved by athletes across Tokyo.
Yoyogi Park served as the Olympic Village site for the 1964 Tokyo Summer Games.
Meiji Shrine is surrounded by an enchanting evergreen forest containing over one hundred thousand donated trees.
Tokyo is exceptionally safe, clean, and pedestrian-friendly, making it a dream destination for runners worldwide.
The historic Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa is Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple, founded in 645 AD.
